newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia mid-year cocoa harvest seen sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia mid-year cocoa harvest seen sharply lower.

text.p: Key cocoa growers in Malaysia said on Tuesday they expected a sharply lower mid-year harvest in 1997 due to rains which ravaged early fruit-setting on cocoa trees.
But the Malaysian Cocoa Board said it was still hoping for a decent harvest of cocoa beans by the end of the year based on encouraging signs at a few plantations using new high-yielding cocoa plants.
Growers in Tawau, the main cocoa growing area in Malaysia's eastern Sabah state, said torrential rains in December had wiped out most of the fruiting for the mid-year crop.
Growers polled by Reuters said production for the April/May/June harvest could be 50 to 60 percent lower than the same period a year ago.
"I think it's going to be an ultra-low mid-year crop," said a Tawau cocoa plantation director, who declined to be named.

He said output from his plantation for the first three months of this year was 15 tonnes while production for the peak April and May months was forecast at nine tonnes, bringing the five-month total to an estimated 24 tonnes.
This was 65 percent lower compared than the 61 tonnes harvested during the first five months of last year, he said.

Another factor hampering production was the growing number of cocoa growers switching to palm oil and other lucrative crops. Plantation officials said the current average bean price of 3,340 ringgit per tonne was not viable for most growers, who were expecting at least 3,800 ringgit a tonne.
A cocoa trader said the lower crop will crimp the supply of cocoa beans on the local market and pressure the 12 grinders in the country to source beans of lesser quality, mostly from Indonesia.
"The grinders are already fighting for whatever beans that are left in the market now," added the trader. Tawau cocoa beans are among the world's best, said industry sources.

Cocoa board chief Mohamed Musa Jamil said he could not make projections on the mid-year crop, but added that the board was hoping for a harvest of around 120,000 tonnes for 1997. Last year's harvest totaled 122,000 tonnes.
Malaysia's next major cocoa harvest is between October and December.
"We have seen some encouraging fruiting in a few Tawau plantations using the new high-yielding clones after the December rains," Mohamed Musa said.
He said for the long-term, the board was expecting a yield of 1.5 tonnes of beans from each hectare of rehabilitated plantations. The current yield rate is 0.5-0.6 tonnes.
Malaysia has about 200,000 hectares under cocoa.
